absent: Exact bit layout and numeric values of allocation flags and watermark modes beyond names observed.
Complete structure layouts and lifecycles for cache and node and slab and extension state beyond fields touched here.
Calling context and sleep and interrupt rules for pre and post hooks beyond node exclusion observed.
Zonelist construction and cpuset and policy node resolution semantics owned elsewhere.
Sanitizer and leak detector and fence and profiling hook effects beyond presence of calls.
Memgroup stock and charge and reparent and LRU accounting semantics beyond failure handling shown.
Diagnostic rate limit parameters and ordering helpers and atomic accessor guarantees owned elsewhere.

findings.text: Allocation entry applies a global allowed mask to the request flags and rejects the request when fault injection is armed for the cache. Bootstrap and explicitly non failing requests bypass injection, as do requests whose reclaim attributes are configured to be ignored and caches lacking the failure testing marker when filtering is active. Warning suppression in the request propagates into the injection decision.

Post allocation entry processes a batch of returned objects by applying sanitizer tagging, optional zeroing, leak tracking when spinning is permitted, additional sanitizer accounting, allocation profiling, and memgroup charging. Success of the whole batch depends on the memgroup step, with single object failure nulling the slot and multi object failure releasing the batch.

Reserve memory access for slab use is granted only when allocation flags indicate eligibility. Explicit denial always fails, explicit memalloc allowance always succeeds, and serving contexts with the memalloc task marker succeed. Otherwise non interrupt context consults the memalloc marker or out of memory victim status, with additional thread flag gating on systems without address translation.

Removal of a single object from a partial slab is valid only while node list exclusion is held. The slab head link supplies the object and the used count advances. Optional consistency validation may reject an invalid slab. Debug processing failure detaches the slab from partial membership and reports failure. Reaching full occupancy moves the slab from partial to full membership.

Whether fresh slab memory is zeroed depends on a global default branch and per cache attributes. When the default is active, caches with constructors never request init, caches marked typesafe or poisoned request init only when the caller asked for zeroed memory, and remaining caches always request init. When the default is inactive, init is requested only when the caller asked for zeroed memory.

Search for partial slabs on other nodes is probabilistically gated by a remote defrag ratio and a cycle derived sample, with a disabled ratio always skipping the search. When attempted, the search walks a zonelist derived from slab policy and allocation scope, considers only nodes with partial counts above a minimum and allowed by cpuset, and retries on concurrent mems changes only when spinning is permitted, otherwise performing a single pass.

Exhaustion reporting is rate limited and suppressed when the caller asked to silence warnings. When emitted, it describes the failing processor and nodes, the cache name and sizing and ordering, a possible debug induced order inflation hint, and per node totals for slabs and objects plus an estimate of free objects in partial slabs. An alternate build provides an empty reporting operation.

Free object estimation in partial slabs is exact for short lists by summing per slab spare capacity under exclusion. For long lists it samples a bounded number of slabs from both ends, scales the sample by the ratio of total partial slabs to slabs scanned, and clamps the result to the node object total.

Intake from a fresh slab caps the request to slab capacity and records fully consumed slabs as needing no partial membership. Objects are drawn through an iterator and the remainder link structure is rebuilt. Partially consumed slabs join the partial list at the head under node exclusion, with accounting for slabs and objects on the owning node.

Node partial list membership and per slab occupancy are guarded by the node list lock with interrupt state preserved. Single object removal asserts the lock is already held. Free estimation holds it across list traversal. Fresh slab insertion acquires it in blocking mode when spinning is allowed and by try acquisition otherwise, discarding the fresh slab on contention without exposing its objects.

Strict NUMA handling redirects only unspecified node requests when a strict branch is active and the caller has a policy. Bind policies keep the local node when it belongs to the permitted set and otherwise resolve the slab policy node. Non bind policies resolve the slab policy node directly.

Zeroing length uses the originally requested size when the cache tracks it, including red zone awareness, and otherwise uses full object size. Integrated sanitizer init can replace explicit zeroing when debug is inactive. Fence protected addresses are excluded from explicit zeroing, and leak tracking occurs only when spinning is permitted.

Allocation profiling is skipped entirely when disabled at runtime, when the object is absent, when the cache opts out of extensions or leak tracing, or when recursion is forbidden. Otherwise an extension vector is ensured or reused, referenced across tag association with the current tag and cache size, and released. Missing extensions mark the current tag inaccurate unless the address belongs to fence testing. An alternate build provides an empty hook.

Memgroup post processing succeeds immediately when memgroup accounting is offline, when neither the request nor the cache asks for accounting, or when the detailed charging step succeeds. On charging failure a single object request aborts that object and nulls the slot, while larger batches release all objects through bulk free.

Detailed memgroup charging bypasses root or absent groups and absent single objects, masks flags to an allowed set, and ensures list LRU state when a LRU is associated. Each object ensures an extension vector except for fence addresses, consumes per processor stock or charges directly with remainder refill, accounts stock against the slab node with a cache specific index, and attaches a referenced group pointer under extension reference.

A slab begins empty and either remains outside partial membership when fully consumed at intake or joins partial membership at the head. Partial membership persists across allocations until the used count meets capacity, at which point the slab leaves partial membership and enters full membership. Debug failures remove the slab from partial membership without entering full membership.

Observed cache node state comprises a list lock, a partial list with a partial count, and slab and object totals. Observed slab state comprises a freelist head, a used count, and a capacity. Observed cache sizing comprises object size, buffer size, orderings, names, defrag ratio, and minimum partial threshold. Observed LRU shard state comprises a list head, a lock, and an item count.

List LRU memgroup allocation succeeds immediately when the LRU is not memgroup aware or the group already has storage, including negative identifiers treated as already present. Otherwise it backfills the farthest unpopulated ancestor toward the target, allocating a single vector once and storing it under indexed exclusion with dying checks and allocation failure retry, freeing any unused vector afterward.

Per group LRU storage is allocated as a flex array sized by the system node count and each node shard is initialized with an empty list, an unlocked spin primitive, a zeroed item count, and an optional lock class derived from the parent LRU key.

Current object group selection returns no group in non maskable context when configured unsafe for such use. Task context prefers an explicitly active memgroup chain, else a cached task group with pending update handling, falling back to a per node root group. Non task context prefers a per processor active group, else the per node root group. Active chain lookup returns the nearest ancestor with populated per node storage.

Pending object group update atomically clears the cached pointer and releases the prior group, returns absent for kernel threads or tasks without address space, looks up the current task memgroup object group under read side protection, and conditionally publishes the new pointer, repeating the whole sequence when a concurrent update raced.

Reading of mems allowed state uses a primitive that is unsafe in non maskable context and is therefore avoided entirely when spinning is forbidden. Concurrent cpuset updates during remote partial search are treated as a harmless race without retry validation on success. Victim reserve access additionally requires a per thread dying marker on systems without address translation.

Node iteration visits every possible node identifier and yields only nodes with populated cache state. Slab and object totals are observed through atomic long reads in one build, while an alternate build reports a constant slab total. These accessors support diagnostics and threshold checks without exposing update paths.

Indexed LRU storage insertion serializes check and store under indexed exclusion with interrupt state preserved, skipping stores for dying groups and retrying when indexed allocation reports shortage of memory. Per shard list mutation is guarded by a dedicated shard lock initialized alongside the list and count, optionally carrying a shared lock class.

Failure to create a slab extension vector emits a single warning and proceeds without profiling or charging for the affected object rather than failing allocation. Fence testing addresses never trigger extension creation and are excluded from inaccurate marking and from charging, leaving their accounting to separate handling.
